---
title: "What the AI wrote, and can we trust it?"
subtitle: "How often the AI cites its sources, where those sources came from, and what still needs a human eye"
---

```{r}
source("_common.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
# Questions left out of the averages are left out here too.
trace <- if (!is.null(trace)) trace[trace$question_id %in% usable_q, , drop = FALSE] else NULL
has_ai <- !is.null(trace) && nrow(trace) > 0
if (has_ai) {
  tr <- trace
  pooled <- do.call(rbind, lapply(conds, function(c) {
    x <- tr[tr$condition == c, ]
    data.frame(condition = c, answers = nrow(x), sentences = sum(x$sentences),
               cited = sum(round(x$cited_share * x$sentences)), invalid = sum(x$invalid_citations),
               uncited = sum(x$uncited_claims), trend = sum(x$trend_sentences),
               trend_cited = sum(round(x$trend_cited_share * x$trend_sentences), na.rm = TRUE),
               cited_records = sum(x$cited_records),
               exp_dep = sum(x$cited_expansion_dependent_share * x$cited_records, na.rm = TRUE),
               not_in_A = sum(x$cited_not_in_A_share * x$cited_records, na.rm = TRUE))
  }))
  tot_sent <- sum(pooled$sentences); tot_inv <- sum(pooled$invalid)
}
```

::: {.in-short}
`r if (has_ai) paste0("**In short.** The AI wrote ", sum(pooled$answers), " answers, ", num(tot_sent), " sentences in all. ", pct(sum(pooled$cited) / tot_sent), " of the sentences cite at least one record. ", if (tot_inv == 0) "None of its citations named a record the AI had not been given" else paste0("Of all its citations, only ", tot_inv, " named a record the AI had not been given"), ": when it cites, it cites real evidence, and it is open about the limits of what it saw. **A citation is not proof, though.** Whether each cited record really supports its sentence can only be judged by people, and that is the next step.") else "**This run has no AI answers.** Run the study with the openai (or anthropic) option to fill this page."`
:::

## Checkers: please stop here

This page shows which search produced each sentence. If you are judging sentences for the
study, please come back after you have finished.
:::

## What the AI was asked to do

For each search, the AI received the **top 8 records** and the research question, and these
rules:

- use only the records given; do not invent records, dates, people or places;
- keep what the records *show* separate from your *interpretation*;
- say when the evidence is too thin, and do not claim a trend from a few records;
- end every sentence about the records with the numbers of the records that support it.

## How well does it cite?

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_ai
p <- pooled
out <- data.frame(Search = cond_short[p$condition], Answers = p$answers, Sentences = p$sentences,
                  `With a citation` = pct(p$cited / p$sentences),
                  `Citations to records not given` = p$invalid,
                  `Sentences without citation` = p$uncited,
                  `Sentences about change` = p$trend,
                  `... of which cited` = ifelse(p$trend > 0, pct(p$trend_cited / p$trend), "-"),
                  check.names = FALSE)
tbl(out)
```

What the columns mean:

- **With a citation**: the sentence names at least one record.
- **Citations to records not given**: the AI named a record number it never received, which
  means it made it up. This should be zero.
- **Sentences without citation**: sentences with no record number that are *not* simply
  remarks about the evidence (such as "the sample is small"). These deserve a closer look:
  they may be unsupported interpretation.
- **Sentences about change**: sentences with words like *shift*, *increase* or *became*. Claims
  about change over time are the riskiest, so we check whether they are backed by records.

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_ai
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-alt: "Dot chart: share of AI sentences with a citation, per question and search."
cs <- reshape(trace[, c("question_id", "condition", "cited_share")], idvar = "question_id", timevar = "condition", direction = "wide")
names(cs) <- sub("cited_share.", "", names(cs), fixed = TRUE)
for (c in conds) if (!c %in% names(cs)) cs[[c]] <- NA
dot_chart(cs, "Share of sentences with a citation", xlim = c(0, 1), order_ids = intersect(qids, cs$question_id))
```
<p class="how-to-read">How to read this: each row is a question, each dot the AI answer for one
search. Further right means more of its sentences cite records.</p>

## Where did the cited records come from?

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_ai
w <- data.frame(Search = cond_short[pooled$condition], `Records cited` = pooled$cited_records,
                `Found only through new words` = pct(pooled$exp_dep / pooled$cited_records),
                `Not found by search A` = pct(pooled$not_in_A / pooled$cited_records), check.names = FALSE)
tbl(w)
```

**What it means.** The answers for search C lean heavily on records that our own words would
never have shown: `r if (has_ai) pct(pooled$not_in_A[3] / pooled$cited_records[3]) else "-"`
of the records it cites were **not found by search A**, and
`r if (has_ai) pct(pooled$exp_dep[3] / pooled$cited_records[3]) else "-"` were found **only**
through words added by Annif or the thesaurus. So the search step does not just change the
list of records. It changes the **story the AI tells**, because the story is built from
different evidence.

## An example

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_ai
a <- answers[answers$question_id == "women-advertising" & answers$condition == "A_direct", "answer"]
if (length(a) && !is.na(a)) {
  lines <- strsplit(a, "\n")[[1]]
  lines <- lines[nzchar(trimws(lines))]
  cat("The first lines of the answer for **", qname("women-advertising"), "**, search A:\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(":::: {.answer-md}\n", md_fix(esc(paste(head(lines, 4), collapse = "\n"))), "\n::::\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

The AI separates what the catalogue records **say** (*"catalogued with subjects including ..."*)
from its own **interpretation**, and it repeatedly warns that metadata is not the same as the
image or text itself. That is the behaviour we asked for. It does not make the
interpretations correct.

## What we cannot tell yet

- whether each cited record really supports its sentence;
- whether the interpretations (for example "a shift from political to commercial contexts")
  hold up;
- whether answers built on search C are better or worse than those built on search A.

These are exactly the questions the two checkers answer on their sheets. See
[Human checking](human-check.qmd).

## Read all the answers

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_ai
for (q in qids) {
  aq <- answers[answers$question_id == q & !is.na(answers$answer), ]
  if (!nrow(aq)) next
  cat(sprintf("\n::: {.callout-note collapse=\"true\" appearance=\"simple\"}\n## %s\n\n", qname(q)))
  for (c in conds) {
    r <- aq[aq$condition == c, ]
    if (!nrow(r)) next
    # Headings inside answers become bold lines; the answer is shown as normal text.
    txt <- gsub("(?m)^#+\\s*(.*)$", "**\\1**", r$answer, perl = TRUE)
    txt <- gsub(":::", ": : :", txt, fixed = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf('<span class="cond cond-%s">%s</span>\n\n:::: {.answer-md}\n%s\n::::\n\n',
                tolower(substr(c, 1, 1)), cond_long[c], md_fix(esc(txt))))
  }
  cat(":::\n")
}
```
